entries.summary: Four Pungs or Kongs and a pair using honours and, if used, 1s or 9s from one suit.

entries.whySpecial: This named hand has its own rules for sets, honours and exposure.
entries.referenceNote: The score and exposure eligibility are calculated under these rules. An exposed Chow does not count.

entries.summary: Three hands share a 1-9 run in one suit. Their honour Pung or Kong and pair tell them apart.

entries.whatItMeans: Guardian Winds uses a Wind meld and Wind pair; Guardian Dragons uses a Dragon meld and Dragon pair; Dragon's Tail deliberately mixes the honour families, one as the meld and the other as the pair.
entries.whySpecial: The same suited run supports three hands with different honour rules.

entries.whySpecial: All four Winds are pairs, while the Dragons make the two sets.

entries.whatItMeans: Chinese Odds is a usual grouped hand in one suit. Odds & Evens spreads odd ranks across two suits and even ranks across the third.

entries.whatItMeans: All three suits must be represented, but the four Chow slots cannot be distributed evenly; one suit supplies two of them.
entries.whySpecial: The four Chows use one suit twice and the other suits once each.

entries.whatItMeans: The three suited melds are parallel versions of one another, differing only by suit; an honour meld and pair complete the hand.
entries.whySpecial: The same number appears as a set in every suit.

entries.whySpecial: The run-and-pair pattern combines a Red Dragon set with your seat Wind set.

facetDefinitions.ordinary-grouped: Qualifying structure uses the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair decomposition.
facetDefinitions.irregular-hand: Qualifying structure does not use the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair decomposition.
facetDefinitions.event-defined: The winning event/context is essential to qualification.
facetDefinitions.one-suit: Qualifying suited tiles come from one numbered suit; honours may still be permitted or required.
facetDefinitions.multiple-suits: The qualifying structure explicitly uses more than one numbered suit.
facetDefinitions.pairs: Pairs are an essential structural feature.
facetDefinitions.pungs-kongs: Pungs and/or Kongs are essential structural features.
facetDefinitions.chow-involving: A Chow is required or explicitly permitted by the reviewed variant.
facetDefinitions.honours: Wind and/or Dragon tiles are structurally required.
facetDefinitions.knitted-interleave: Same-number tiles across suits form the defining interleaved structure.
facetDefinitions.green-tiles: Composition is restricted to Green Dragon and the permitted green Bamboo tiles.
facetDefinitions.rank-parity: Odd/even suited-rank membership is a defining qualification fact.
facetDefinitions.parallel-ranks: The same suited rank is deliberately repeated across multiple suits as corresponding groups.
facetDefinitions.mixed-chow: A three-tile group with one tile from each suit whose ranks form one consecutive three-rank run; unlike an ordinary Chow, the tiles do not share a suit.
facetDefinitions.hybrid-layout: Represented melds and a separate loose structural component share one hand example.
